data.title: Explore Life in Pioneer Times
data.description: Students will explore what everyday life was like for pioneers and decide whether certain details belong to the past, today, or both.

priorEra.name: Early Colonial Days
priorEra.body: Before the western wagon trails were fully open, settlers lived in smaller eastern towns closer to the coast. Travel was even slower, mostly relying on small sailboats and horse trails instead of covered wagons.

lenses.title: Daily Life
lenses.body: Pioneer families lived in simple log cabins built by hand with few or no windows. They woke up before sunrise to start a fire in the hearth for heat and cooking. Water had to be carried in buckets from a nearby stream or hand-dug well.

lenses.title: Technology
lenses.body: Families did not have electricity, running water, or gas stoves. Instead, they relied on candles and oil lamps for light and heavy iron pots over an open fire to cook meals. Traveling long distances required walking, riding horses, or bumping along in covered wagons.

lenses.title: School & Work
lenses.body: Children helped their parents with heavy daily chores like gathering firewood, feeding farm animals, and weeding the vegetable garden. When they went to school, all the students of different ages sat together in a single room with one teacher.

challenges.statement: Children help their families by gathering firewood and feeding farm animals every single day.
challenges.explanation: Children have always had important chores to help support their families, both in pioneer times and today.

challenges.statement: Families turn on a kitchen faucet to get clean running water instantly for cooking and washing.
challenges.explanation: Indoor plumbing with running water is a modern convenience that pioneer families did not have in their log cabins.

challenges.statement: Students of all different ages study together in a small one-room schoolhouse with a single teacher.
challenges.explanation: Pioneer communities were small, so all grades shared one room and one teacher instead of going to large modern schools.

challenges.statement: People travel across the country by bumping along slowly in heavy covered wagons pulled by oxen.
challenges.explanation: Pioneers had to rely on animal-drawn wagons because cars, trains, and airplanes had not been invented yet.

challenges.statement: Children play games, run around outdoors, and spend time laughing with their friends.
challenges.explanation: Playing and having fun with friends is something children do in every time period, past and present.
